name: MACE foundation models (MACE-MP-0 and successors)
origin_detail: MACE code by Ilyes Batatia, Gregor Simm, David Kovacs and 'the group of Gabor Csanyi, and friends' (ACEsuit). The MACE-MP-0 paper has 88 authors. The Cambridge affiliation is widely reported but not stated on fetched pages.

licences.weights: MIT (MP-0 family, MPA-0); Academic Software License, non-commercial (OMAT-0, MATPES-0, OMOL-0, MH-0/1, MDP, OFF23)
licences.data: trained on open datasets (MPtrj, sAlex, OMat24, MATPES, OMol25, SPICE)

openness_notes: Code MIT. MACE-MP-0 (a, b, b2, b3) and MPA-0 (MPtrj + sAlex) weights are MIT. Newer foundation models (OMAT-0, MATPES-PBE-0, MATPES-r2SCAN-0, OMOL-0, MH-0/1 and MDP) are under the ASL, which is 'for academic non-commercial use only', reciprocal, and directs commercial users to 'obtain a commercial use license'. MACE-OFF23 is also ASL. The training data are all public; OMat24 and OMol25 are CC BY 4.0, so the ASL is the developers' choice and not inherited (Orb trains Apache-2.0 models on the same data). Release dates of the ASL models are not shown; they need MACE v0.3.10 to v0.3.16. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Initial 4 (MIT code and weights, open MPtrj data); current 2 (the newest flagship models are non-commercial).

license_history.license: Academic Software License (OMAT-0, MATPES-0, OMOL-0, MH-0/1, MDP)
license_history.note: Require MACE v0.3.10-v0.3.16; dates not shown.

relicensing_events.to: Academic Software License (non-commercial) for later foundation models
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Older MIT models stay available. Commercial users must buy a licence or use rival open models trained on the same CC BY data. Year not confirmed (after OMat24, Oct 2024).

risk_events: Non-commercial licence on newest models limits industrial uptake
robustness: MIT code and MIT MP-0/MPA-0 weights remain; training data public, so anyone can retrain.
physical_science_relevance: Universal atomistic simulation across the periodic table; a widely used academic MLIP family.
openness_effect_assessment: The MIT MACE-MP-0 helped establish universal MLIPs as open tools: 1.4k stars and an 88-author validation paper. Moving later models to a non-commercial licence follows the open-core pattern seen in startups, though here the motive is presumably institutional licensing income (not confirmed).
key_takeaway: Academic does not always mean permissive. The same group publishes MIT and non-commercial models. Licence choice for models trained on CC BY data is unconstrained, so it reflects the developer's commercialisation strategy.
